Title: August 27, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Study Session - Excel Energy Partnership Update and Wildfire Resilience
Overview: At the August 27, 2026 Boulder City Council study session, Excel Energy reported on its 2020 franchise and energy partnership, including about 60% emissions reductions by the end of 2025 and wildfire mitigation work such as undergrounding three feeders and a two-phase transmission rebuild, while council pressed on outages, restoration communication, rates, and customer service. Staff then presented a draft home hardening hub, a project inventory of about 137 projects, and a draft risk index dividing the western wildland-urban interface into 12 sections, and council asked about contractors, renters, funding, and measurable 2030 targets. No formal decisions were made; staff committed to follow-up responses and a return to council in October.

Topic1.Title: Excel Energy Partnership Update
Topic1.Summary: Excel Energy presented progress under the 2020 franchise and energy partnership agreement, including 100% emissions-free electricity goals, 85% carbon-free by 2030, and emissions reductions of about 60% achieved by end of 2025. Excel described wildfire mitigation work, including AI panel cameras, enhanced power line safety settings, undergrounding of three feeders, and a transmission rebuild in two phases. Council members pressed on frequent outages, restoration communication, rate impacts, rolling outage risk, and customer service issues.

Topic2.Title: Wildfire Resilience Home Hardening Hub and Mitigation Priorities
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented a council priority project on wildfire resilience, including a draft home hardening implementation hub to connect homeowners to guidance, incentives, and mitigation actions. Staff also presented a project inventory of about 137 projects grouped into 25 programs, 10 tier one priorities, and a draft WOOI risk index dividing the western wildland-urban interface into 12 sections. Council asked about contractor lists, renter participation, mandatory retroactive home hardening, funding models, and measurable 2030 targets.

Topic3.Title: Public Comment and Council Questions Closing
Topic3.Summary: Council members gave short closing comments to Excel and staff, emphasizing reliability, transparency, customer service, and the need for measurable goals. Staff committed to follow-up responses and an October return for further discussion.
